subject: Service accounts, JWT rotation & routing — post-demo tech clarifications
messages:
From: Alice Gomez <alice@finlytics.io>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Cc: Bob Chu <bch@finlytics.io>, security@finlytics.io
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 16:05:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — follow-up items (service accounts + routing)

Thanks for the demo earlier — it was helpful. A couple quick follow-ups from our engineering team:

1) For our regulated workloads we want service accounts per product environment (dev/staging/prod). Can you confirm Redwood supports issuing scoped service-account credentials (not long-lived master API keys)? Prefer OAuth/JWT with short-lived tokens and automatic refresh.

2) Key rotation: What are the options for us? Ideally rotation without downtime and a CI-friendly workflow (rotate via KMS + publish to our vault).

3) Routing/regions: We want traffic for EU customers to stay in eu-west-1 and fall back to us-only models when capacity is constrained. How granular is the routing policy API?

Appreciate concise answers; we need to include this in the internal security review next week.

—Alice

From: lauren_bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Alice Gomez <alice@finlytics.io>, Bob Chu <bch@finlytics.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — follow-up items (service accounts + routing)

Hi Alice — great to keep this moving. Short answers and next steps below; attaching a suggested MAP (MVP_MAP_v1.docx) and a short spec (redwood-jwt-patterns.pdf).

1) Service accounts / auth patterns
- Redwood supports customer-managed service accounts with scoped credentials. We recommend ephemeral JWTs minted by your IAM role and exchanged at the Redwood auth endpoint for short-lived tokens (default TTL 15m). Long-lived API keys are supported but should be treated as legacy; we can scope and restrict them per environment for compatibility.
- We offer a service-account model (serviceAccountId) you can create via the Admin API. Each service account can be bound to roles and allowed models/endpoints.

2) Key rotation
- Rotation without downtime: Redwood supports phased key swaps: you can upload a new public key (or new API key) and mark it active at a chosen timestamp; until the activation time both keys can be accepted. We also integrate with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and Vault for automatic secrets provisioning.
- CI-friendly: we expose endpoints for rotating keys and publishing metadata (key IDs) so you can rotate from your pipeline and signal a canary rollout. We'll share a sample GitHub Actions snippet in the Drive link.

3) Routing/regions
- Routing policies are policy objects you control: by region, latency SLA, cost tier. You can pin traffic by account, route by request attributes (geo header, tenant ID), and specify fallbacks (model variants or region). The API supports per-route fallbacks and weighted rollouts.

Next steps
- I propose a short tech sync with Rishi to map your IAM and Vault layout (30 min). I'll also share the MAP and a small reproducible auth example. Can you confirm availability for Mon/Tue this week?

Thanks,
Lauren

Thanks Lauren — that's very helpful. A couple clarifications before we schedule:

- TTL 15m for tokens sounds good. Do you publish a discovery endpoint for the auth token rotation metadata (jwks_uri) so our services can validate tokens locally?

- For the phased key swap: does the Admin API require any downtime on active streams, or can active sessions continue using the old key until explicit cutover?

- Regarding model fallbacks: will we be able to programmatically examine model variant cost/latency profiles to automate fallback decisions?

If we can get short answers to those three items we'll sign off with security and pick a slot for the tech sync.

Best,
Bob

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Bob Chu <bch@finlytics.io>, Alice Gomez <alice@finlytics.io>

Date: Sun, 29 Nov 2026 11:42:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Redwood demo — follow-up items (service accounts + routing)

Hi Bob/Alice — quick technical clarifications from the infra side:

- jwks_uri / token discovery: yes. We publish a jwks_uri per region (and per customer for private deployments) so you can validate JWTs without calling the auth endpoint for each request. The discovery doc also includes active_kids and rotation window metadata.

- Phased key swap behavior: active sessions that present a token signed with the previous key will continue to be accepted until the key replay window closes (configurable; default 10 minutes). We also support session-level token introspection for stricter enforcement.

- Model variant profiles: Redwood exposes a /metrics/model-profile endpoint that returns per-variant latency and cost estimates (p50/p95 token latency, cost-per-1k-tokens). You can query this programmatically and build logic for automated fallback or weighted routing.

I'll prepare a short post with the example curl snippets and the GitHub Actions rotation workflow; can provide in the Drive folder by EOD.

-r
